data: We have 100 tons, and leaving 50 means the lake returns to 100 next month. I propose this month’s catches: 14 tons for me and 9 each for John, Kate, Jack, and Emma—50 total. I’m asking for the larger share, but everyone else would still earn $9,000 while preserving a full lake for next month. John, would you accept 9 tons under that allocation, or what split would you propose?

Luke, keeping the total at 50 tons makes sense, but why should you get 14 while everyone else gets 9? I learned to fish here with my family, and I want this lake to keep supporting all our families. I propose 10 tons each: equal income of $10,000 and enough fish left to restore the lake next month. We can check the revealed catches afterward and keep that agreement going. John, would you support an equal split?

I’m with Emma: I’ll commit to 10 tons if we all agree to the same limit. My family taught me to leave enough fish for the next season, and a fair split gives us a plan we can keep month after month. Luke, will you join us at 10 tons? John and Jack, can you commit too?

Count me in for 10 tons. That’s $10,000 each this month without taking away next month’s livelihood. Let’s review the revealed catches together afterward and stick with equal shares while the lake stays full. Luke, will you accept 10 tons too? We still need John’s agreement.

I’m in for 10 tons. An equal share protects both our incomes and the lake our families depend on. Luke, four of us support this split—will you join us at 10 so we can all start with the same agreement?
